reasoning: The failure is a collision with a low-profile stationary obstacle (a small rover parked in front of a bin) while approaching at ~0.75 m/s on flat concrete. Because the IMU log was corrupted, exact speed and distances were estimated visually, creating uncertainty in `observed_speed`, `obs_x`, `obs_y`, and `obs_r`. Furthermore, to ensure the policy robustly avoids stationary obstacles across realistic variations of this encounter (including front-left, center, and front-right impacts, varied obstacle sizes like scooters or bins, and different stopping distances/surfaces), we randomize obstacle position (`obs_x`, `obs_y`), obstacle radius (`obs_r`), approach speed (`observed_speed`), ego lateral offset (`lateral_offset`), and surface friction (`friction`).

ranges.why: Account for visual estimation uncertainty around 1.8 m and test obstacle detection/braking across shorter (1.2 m) and longer (2.6 m) reaction distances.
Vary lateral position from -0.40 m (right-side clip) through center (0.0 m) to +0.20 m (left-side clip) so the policy cannot just swerve blindly in one direction.
Cover smaller low-profile obstacles (0.12 m radius, like scooter wheels) up to wider bins or larger rovers (0.35 m radius).
Sensor speed was unknown due to corrupted logs; sampling 0.50 to 1.20 m/s covers the visual estimate (~0.75 m/s) and higher speeds that challenge braking distance.
Simulate slight variations in the robot's initial curving trajectory and alignment relative to the obstacle.
Vary from dusty/damp concrete (0.6) to high-grip dry pavement (1.1) so braking and swerving maneuvers remain reliable.
